newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher, driven up by chip shares.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher, driven up by chip shares.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed higher on Wednesday, mainly encouraged by institutional investors' buying in the semiconductor sector. But many brokers said that the chip market has not yet bottomed out and that it was not likely to continue keeping the whole market afloat.
The key Nikkei 225 average gained 178.68 points or 0.84 percent to close at 21,350.67. Its December futures gained 210 points to end at 21,370.
"What led the stock market higher today were semiconductor-related shares," said a broker at a major Japanese securities house.
NEC Corp shares gained 60 yen to end at 1,290 yen, marking the heaviest trading volume in the first section.
Fujitsu Ltd, which had the third-largest volume, was up 31 yen to close at 1,030 yen.
Toshiba Corp shares climbed 36 yen to end at 741 yen on the fifth heaviest volume.
Shares of pharmaceutical maker Eisai Co Ltd rose after the company said it would release information on authorities' approval of a product it is developing.
Eisai's share price was up 50 yen to close at 2,070 yen.

In the over-the-counter (OTC) market, shares in Olympic Sports Co were ask-only, after the Japan Securities Dealers Association (JSDA) said on Friday that it had cancelled the firm's registration on the OTC market.
The share price was ask-only at 311 yen by the end of the day. The shares were last traded on Thursday at 471 yen.
The OTC index was down 4.08 points or 0.26 percent at 1,554.09.
The second section index was down 0.21 points or 0.01 percent to end at 2,091.42, with 8.39 million shares traded.
